clue.text: Extracts taken out of Italian literary works

indicators.note: the word for extracts has taken something in, holding it inside itself

blocks.note: wrings, as in wrings a confession out of someone
It is the crossword abbreviation for Italian (vermouth)

explanation.surface: A scholar lifts passages from the great works of Italian literature for an anthology.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Extracts' as a noun, quotations; in the wordplay it is a verb, as in forcing something out of someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Writings are written compositions, so literary works is a direct synonym for the plural noun.

clue.text: A bit of an old woman? Much appreciated though!

definitions.text: A bit of an old woman? Much appreciated though!

blocks.clueFragment: A bit of an old woman?
blocks.note: surface reading: some part of an elderly lady's body
setter's reading: a small coin given by a poor widow in the Gospels, praised by Jesus above richer gifts

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit' is a small coin, and the old woman is the poor widow of Mark 12 who gave her last two mites; Jesus valued it above the rich men's offerings.
explanation.definitionFit: The widow's mite is a small gift from someone with little, valued because of its sacrifice.

clue.text: Obscure language must be restricted by tabloid, obviously

indicators.note: restricted by means held within the bounds of the words that follow

blocks.note: the end of tabloid and the start of obviously

explanation.surface: Newspapers that print strange jargon will obviously be reined in.
explanation.definitionFit: Ido is an artificial language derived from Esperanto, spoken by very few people, hence obscure.

clue.text: Painter's entrance

blocks.note: first meaning: belonging to Ingres, the French painter, written with the possessive
second meaning: a way in, or the act of going in

explanation.walkthrough: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a 19th-century French painter; add the possessive and you get the word for a way in.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingress is a formal word for entering or the right to enter, the opposite of egress.

clue.text: Stomach medicine in a glass butler brought out

indicators.note: the words are brought out of their order and set out afresh

blocks.note: all twelve letters of these three words

explanation.surface: The butler brings in a glass of something for an upset stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stomach' looks like the verb to tolerate, but here it is the organ the medicine treats.
explanation.definitionFit: Glauber's salt, sodium sulphate, was long taken as a laxative, a remedy for the digestive system.

clue.text: Set time gets a vote of approval

blocks.note: to set something down is to place it
T is the usual abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A meeting agrees its schedule by a show of hands.
explanation.walkthrough: Placet, Latin for 'it pleases', is the word used to vote yes in some university and church assemblies.
explanation.definitionFit: In formal assemblies a placet is an affirmative vote, the Latin assent recorded in favour of a motion.

clue.text: The woman's in front position but restricted

indicators.note: in places the woman inside the word for front position

blocks.note: to be in the lead is to be in front
she is the woman; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: She is out in front of the race, yet held back.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'woman's' stands for 'is', so the woman is in LEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog on a leash is held in check, so leashed means restrained or restricted.

clue.text: Talk with a number in classical attire in 17 city

indicators.note: in places the number inside the classical garment

blocks.note: to chat is to talk
the toga was the dress of ancient Romans
taken as written
No. is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: People chat in togas at a classical-themed party in a Tennessee city.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 refers to the answer at 17-across, so the definition is a city in that state.
explanation.definitionFit: Chattanooga is a city in the US state named at 17-across, famous from the Chattanooga Choo Choo song.

clue.text: Monkey — it repeatedly climbs tree

indicators.note: in a down answer, climbing means reading upward, from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
the word repeated once more

explanation.surface: A monkey keeps scrambling up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Both ends define: titi is a small South American monkey and also a shrub or small tree of the southern US.
explanation.definitionFit: The titi is a small South American monkey, and the same name is given to an American flowering tree.

clue.text: Become less ambitious in exploit to score points?

blocks.note: first meaning: to drop a goal, abandoning an aim
second meaning: in rugby, a kick through the posts from a ball dropped to the ground

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase, it means giving up an objective; as a noun, it is a rugby scoring kick worth three points.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop goal is a rugby kick that scores points, and dropping a goal is lowering one's aims.

clue.text: British sailor holed by a rock

indicators.note: something holed has a hole punched in it, and the gap is filled by the next word

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
taken as written
an old salt is an experienced sailor

explanation.surface: A British seaman's ship has been holed by striking a rock.
explanation.walkthrough: B and SALT, the British sailor, have A placed between them. The 'a' before 'rock' does double duty in the surface but serves the wordplay here.
explanation.definitionFit: Basalt is a dark volcanic stone, so it is one example of a rock.

clue.text: Urges to go on mountain peak? Then order food

blocks.note: to egg someone on is to urge them
ben is a Scottish word for mountain, used in peak names like Ben Nevis
an edict is an official order

explanation.surface: A climber reaches the summit and then calls for something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs Benedict is a brunch dish of poached eggs and ham on a muffin with hollandaise, a food.

clue.text: Get a bowler hat, disguised as constitutional expert

indicators.note: a disguise changes how something looks, so these letters appear in a different arrangement

blocks.note: all thirteen letters used as they stand

explanation.surface: Someone puts on a bowler hat to pass as a stuffy constitutional lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'constitutional' is also a health walk, a false trail; Walter Bagehot was the Victorian author of The English Constitution.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagehot's book on the English Constitution made him the classic authority on how the British system of government works.

clue.text: Extant monument one found in Africa

blocks.note: extant means still existing, alive
a memorial stone is a monument

explanation.surface: A surviving memorial stands somewhere in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on Stanley finding the explorer: 'Dr Livingstone, I presume?'
explanation.definitionFit: David Livingstone, the explorer, was famously found by Henry Stanley at Ujiji in 1871.

clue.text: Possibly lead tot in speaking game

indicators.note: speaking means we are going by how the words are said, not spelt

blocks.note: lead is one example of a metal
a tot is a sum added up, as in tot up

explanation.surface: A toddler is being taught a word game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like a pastime, but it is the adjective meaning plucky. 'Tot' looks like a child; here it is a column of figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone game is willing and brave, and mettlesome means full of spirit and courage.

clue.text: Male Hindu god going about as a bird

indicators.note: going about is turning round, as a ship does, so the god's name faces the other way

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for male
Siva, or Shiva, is a principal Hindu deity

explanation.surface: A male Hindu deity takes the form of a bird and flies about.
explanation.definitionFit: Mavis is an old poetic name for the song thrush, a common garden songbird.

clue.text: The White House? One living there edges off to church

indicators.note: with its edges off, a word loses its first and last letters

blocks.note: the US president lives in the White House
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A puzzle about who lives in the White House and how they go to church.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the White House as only one example of the kind of building the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: The White House is the official home of the US president, so it is a residence by example.

clue.text: Name of US dramatist given fanfare on return, look

indicators.note: something on its return comes back the way it went, so the fanfare word is read from the end

blocks.note: a sennet is a trumpet flourish in Elizabethan stage directions
to look is to see

explanation.surface: An American playwright gets a trumpet welcome when he comes home, so take a look.
explanation.walkthrough: Sennet appears in Shakespeare's stage directions, for example 'Sennet. Enter King'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennessee was the first name, a nickname in fact, of the playwright Tennessee Williams.

clue.text: Stirring feelings, putting an end to sensible reason

indicators.note: an end to a word means just its final letter

blocks.note: the final letter of sensible
a motive is the reason for doing something

explanation.surface: Emotions are running high and good sense is abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotive describes something that arouses strong emotion, as in an emotive issue.

clue.text: European beast holding soldiers back

indicators.note: the animal is holding something, with it gripped inside
back means the soldiers are written in the backward direction

blocks.note: a cat is a beast in the broad sense of an animal
OR is 'other ranks', soldiers below officer rank

explanation.surface: A wild animal from Europe keeps an army at bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European beast' looks like one phrase for a European animal, but European alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Croat is a native of Croatia, which is a country in Europe.

clue.text: Series of acts upsetting Dick outside a pub

indicators.note: upsetting in a down clue tips the word over so it reads from bottom to top
outside means the detective wraps around the rest

blocks.note: a dick and a tec are both slang for a detective
taken as written
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A troublemaker causes upset outside a pub where entertainers perform.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret is a nightclub entertainment made up of a sequence of songs, dances and turns.

clue.text: Our lad bled — he's broken a bone

indicators.note: something broken is smashed up, and the letters are put back together in a new order

blocks.note: all thirteen letters, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A parent reports that their boy bled after breaking a bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' does double duty: in the surface he broke a bone, in the wordplay it rearranges the words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The shoulder blade, or scapula, is the flat bone at the back of the shoulder.

clue.text: Show disdain that's just a bit short of malice

indicators.note: a bit short means the word falls one letter shy, missing its tail

blocks.note: spite is malice

explanation.surface: Someone sneers, stopping just short of real cruelty.
explanation.definitionFit: Spitting at someone, or just spitting, is a crude act of contempt, a way of showing scorn.

clue.text: Someone paid needs suitable earnings

blocks.note: a pro, a professional, is paid to play
fit as in fit for purpose

explanation.surface: An employee demands a fair wage.
explanation.definitionFit: Profit is money gained from business, so it serves as a synonym for earnings.

clue.text: Bottle I found drifting — inside being sailor's last text

indicators.note: something drifting moves about aimlessly, so these letters wander into a new order
last asks for only the final letter of the word before it
this says one piece is set inside the other

blocks.note: the seven letters of these two words
the final letter of sailor

explanation.surface: A castaway finds a drifting bottle with a message from a dead sailor inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a message in a bottle; 'text' is the definition at the far end.
explanation.definitionFit: A libretto is the written words of an opera or musical, its text as opposed to its score.

clue.text: Bill finds club uplifting

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting up means the word reads upward

blocks.note: a bat is a club used in cricket or baseball

explanation.surface: A man called Bill finds his club cheering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name; it is the account at a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A tab is a running account or bill, as in picking up the tab at a restaurant.

clue.text: You must restrict extremes of ebullience — only a snigger!

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two end letters
to restrict is to hem in, so one piece is closed inside the other

blocks.note: thee is the old form of you
first and last letters of ebullience

explanation.surface: Someone is told to curb their high spirits and allow themselves no more than a snigger.
explanation.walkthrough: Thee is the archaic object form of you, still heard in hymns and some dialects.
explanation.definitionFit: Tee-hee is the written imitation of a stifled giggle, so it stands for the snigger itself.

clue.text: Army will invade farm building — OK for briefing?

indicators.note: an army that invades goes inside the territory, here a word

blocks.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
a stable is a farm building for horses

explanation.surface: Soldiers are about to storm a barn: is that cleared for the press briefing?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark warns that the definition is loose: a briefing is where things are stated.
explanation.definitionFit: Something statable can be stated, so it is fit to be said in a briefing.
